questions.solution: In the adventivetype of polyembryony, embryos develop directly from the nucellus or integuments. It is seen in is seen in Citrus, Opuntia, and Mangifera.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Sexual reproduction in Spirogyra is an advanced feature because it shows:
options: different sizes of motile sex organs
same size of motile sex organs
questions.solution: In Spirogyra, the sexual reproduction involves the fusion of two morphologically identical isogametes and physiologically dissimilar anisogametes. This is a case of primitive anisogamy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is without exception in angiosperms?
questions.solution: Only angiosperms have double fertilization, in which the secondary nucleus forms a triploid cell to produce endosperm and the egg transforms into a diploid zygote to form embryo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Angiosperms pollen tubes liberate their male gametes into the:
questions.solution:
The male gametes in the pollen tube are discharged into the synergid cells from where the first male gamete is transferred to the egg cell of the embryo sac. The other male gamete is transferred to the central cell through the cytoplasmic current.
Related Theory
Towards the micropylar end, a mature ovule consists of embryo sac which has an egg apparatus (an egg cell and two synergids), centrally placed two polar nuclei and 3 antipodal cells at the chalazal end.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In angiosperm all the four microspores of tetrad are covered by a layer which is formed by:
questions.solution:
Callose wall surrounds the sporocytes during the meiotic stage. It provides an isolation barrier sealing off one meiotic cell (megaspore mother cell) from another.
Related Theory
Tetrad is a group of four haploid and immature pollen grains in tetrahedral fashion produced by meiotic microsporogenesis. The tetrads are of five types namely tetrahedral (most common), isobilateral, $T$ shaped, decussate and linera. In dicots, the most common type of pollen tetrad is tetrahedral.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following fruits, the edible part is the aril?
questions.solution: Litchi is a nut type simple fruit. When a single fruit develops from a single ovary of a single flower, it is called a simple fruit. An aril which is a specialized outgrowth from a seed that partly or completely covers the seed is the edible part of litchi. In custard apple, the berries become very fleshy and being crowded together on a thick thalamus form a complex single fruit. the mesocarp, i.e. the fleshy part is the edible part of custard apple. Pomegranate is a balausta which is a berry with an outer hard rind formed of epicarp and a part of mesocarp. Succulent testa is the edible part of pomegranate. A citrus fruit is berry called a hesperidium that has a thick, leathery rind, with numerous oil glands (juicy placental hair), and a large flesh portion composed of several wedge-shaped sections.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a cereal grain the single cotyledon of embryo is represented by:
questions.solution:
In a cereal grain (e.g., wheat), the single cotyledon of embryo is represented by the scutellum. Scutellum is specialized for nutrient absorption from the endosperm. Coleoptile is a modified ensheathing leaf that covers and protects the young primary leaves of a grass seedling. Coleorhiza is a sheath like structure found on the radicle which covers and protects it during the growth into the soil.
Related Theory
The scutellum is a modified cotyledon, or seed leaf in grasses which never develops into a green structure but serves only to digest endosperm and transfer nutrients to the rest of the embryo. Scutellum is diploid while endosperm is triploid.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The aleurone layer in maize grain is specially rich in:
questions.solution:
The aleurone layer of maize grain is especially rich in proteins in mature seeds and tubers. It forms the outermost layer of the endosperm.
Related Theory
Aleurone lies between the pericarp and the hyaline layer of the endosperm. Unlike the cells of the starchy endosperm, aleurone cells remain alive at maturity. The ploidy of the aleurone is (3n) as a result of double fertilization.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the direction of micropyle in anatropous ovule?
questions.solution:
Anatropous ovule is the most common type of ovule found in angiosperms. Here the ovule is inverted so that micropyle and hilum are present in the same line and the micropyle is directed downwards.
Related Theory
Micropyle is used for the various functions and processes of the egg or the seed plant. It is located at top of the seed or egg. It helps in absorbing the water at the time of germination of the seed. Through micropyle the root emerges out at the time of germination of the seed.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: When does the decision that the plant is going to flower take place?
options: Much before the flower is seen
When the flower is fully developed
After the flower buds are formed
questions.solution: Much before the actual flower is seen on a plant, the decision that the plant is going to flower has taken place. Several hormonal and structural changes are initiated which lead to the differentiation and further development of the floral primordium. Inflorescences are formed which bear the floral buds and then the flowers. In the flower the male and female reproductive structures, the androecium and the gynoecium differentiate and develop. You would recollect that the androecium consists of a whorl of stamens representing the male reproductive organ and the gynoecium represents the female reproductive organ.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What are the two parts of a typical stamen?
questions.solution: the two parts of a typical stamen – the long and slender stalk called the filament, and the terminal generally bilobed structure called the anther. The proximal end of the filament is attached to the thalamus or the petal of the flower. The number and length of stamens are variable in flowers of different species. If you were to collect a stamen each from ten flowers (each from different species) and arrange them on a slide, you would be able to appreciate the large variation in size seen in nature. Careful observation of each stamen under a dissecting microscope and making neat diagrams would elucidate the range in shape and attachment of anthers in different flowers. A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed with each lobe having two theca, i.e., they are dithecous Often a longitudinal groove runs lengthwise separating the theca.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What process leads to the formation of microspore tetrads?
questions.solution: As each cell of the sporogenous tissue is capable of giving rise to a microspore tetrad. Each one is a potential pollen or microspore mother cell. The process of formation of microspores from a pollen mother cell (PMC) through meiosis is called microsporogenesis. The microspores, as they are formed, are arranged in a cluster of four cells–the microspore tetrad As the anthers mature and dehydrate, the microspores dissociate from each other and develop into pollen grains Inside each microsporangium several thousands of microspores or pollen grains are formed that are released with the dehiscence of anther. Pollen grain: The pollen grains represent the male gametophytes. If you touch the opened anthers of Hibiscus or any other flower you would find deposition of yellowish powdery pollen grains on your fingers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which part of the flower represents the female reproductive part?
questions.solution: The gynoecium represents the female reproductive part of the flower. The gynoecium may consist of a single pistil (monocarpellary) or may have more than one pistil (multicarpellary). When there are more than one, the pistils may be fused together (syncarpous) or may be free (apocarpous) Each pistil has three parts the stigma, style and ovary. The stigma serves as a landing platform for pollen grains. The style is the elongated slender part beneath the stigma. The basal bulged part of the pistil is the ovary. Inside the ovary is the ovarian cavity (locule). The placenta is located inside the ovarian cavity. Recall the definition and types of placentation that you studied in Arising from the placenta are the megasporangia, commonly called ovules. The number of ovules in an ovary may be one (wheat, paddy, mango) to many (papaya, water melon, orchids).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What type of division does the nucleus of the functional megaspore undergo?
questions.solution: Let us study about the formation of the embryo sac in detail. The nucleus of the functional megaspore divides mitotically to form two nuclei which move to the opposite poles, forming the 2- nucleate embryo sac. Two more sequential mitotic nuclear divisions result in the formation of the 4-nucleate and later the 8-nucleate stages of the embryo sac. It is of interest to note that these mitotic divisions are strictly free nuclear, that is, nuclear divisions are not followed immediately by cell wall formation. After the 8-nucleate stage, cell walls are laid down leading to the organisation of the typical female gametophyte or embryo sac. Observe the distribution of cells inside the embryo sac Six of the eight nuclei are surrounded by cell walls and organised into cells; the remaining two nuclei, called polar nuclei are situated below the egg apparatus in the large central cell. There is a characteristic distribution of the cells within the embryo sac.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: How common is water pollination among flowering plants?
questions.solution: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons. As against this, you would recall that water is a regular mode of transport for the male gametes among the lower plant groups such as algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes. It is believed, particularly for some bryophytes and pteridophytes, that their distribution is limited because of the need for water for the transport of male gametes and fertilisation. Some examples of water pollinated plants are Vallisneria and Hydrilla which grow in fresh water and several marine sea-grasses such as Zostera. Not all aquatic plants use water for pollination. In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in most of the land plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the primary result of continued self-pollination in flowering plants?
questions.solution: Outbreeding Devices : Majority of flowering plants produce hermaphrodite flowers and pollen grains are likely to come in contact with the stigma of the same flower. Continued self-pollination result in inbreeding depression. Flowering plants have developed many devices to discourage self- pollination and to encourage cross-pollination. In some species, pollen release and stigma receptivity are not synchronised. Either the pollen is released before the stigma becomes receptive or stigma becomes receptive much before the release of pollen. In some other species, the anther and stigma are placed at different positions so that the pollen cannot come in contact with the stigma of the same flower. Both these devices prevent autogamy. The third device to prevent inbreeding is self-incompatibility.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What happens after the pollen tube enters one of the synergids?
options: The pollen tube releases one male gamete into the cytoplasm.
The pollen tube releases two male gametes into the cytoplasm.
The pollen tube fuses with the egg cell.
The pollen tube releases enzymes into the cytoplasm.
questions.solution: After entering one of the synergids, the pollen tube releases the two male gametes into the cytoplasm of the synergid. One of the male gametes moves towards the egg cell and fuses with its nucleus thus completing the syngamy. This results in the formation of a diploid cell, the zygote. The other male gamete moves towards the two polar nuclei located in the central cell and fuses with them to produce a triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN). As this involves the fusion of three haploid nuclei it is termed triple fusion. Since two types of fusions, syngamy and triple fusion take place in an embryo sac the phenomenon is termed double fertilisation, an event unique to flowering plants. The central cell after triple fusion becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into the endosperm while the zygote develops into an embryo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the stage of endosperm development where the PEN undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give rise to free nuclei called?
questions.solution: Endosperm development precedes embryo development. Why? The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly and forms a triploid endosperm tissue. In the most common type of endosperm development, the PEN undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give rise to free nuclei. This stage of endosperm development is called free-nuclear endosperm. Subsequently cell wall formation occurs and the endosperm becomes cellular. The number of free nuclei formed before cellularisation varies greatly. The coconut water from tender coconut that you are familiar with, is nothing but free-nuclear endosperm (made up of thousands of nuclei) and the surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm. Endosperm may either be completely consumed by the developing embryo (e.g., pea, groundnut, beans) before seed maturation or it may persist in the mature seed (e.g. castor and coconut) and be used up during seed germination.

In the most common type of endosperm development, the PEN undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give rise to free nuclei. This stage of endosperm development is called free-nuclear endosperm. Subsequently cell wall formation occurs and the endosperm becomes cellular. The number of free nuclei formed before cellularisation varies greatly. The coconut water from tender coconut that you are familiar with, is nothing but free-nuclear endosperm (made up of thousands of nuclei) and the surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the final product of sexual reproduction in angiosperms?
questions.solution: In angiosperms, the seed is the final product of sexual reproduction. It is often described as a fertilised ovule. Seeds are formed inside fruits. A seed typically consists of seed coat(s), cotyledon(s) and an embryo axis. The cotyledons (Figure 1.15a) of the embryo are simple structures, generally thick and swollen due to storage of food reserves (as in legumes). Mature seeds may be non-albuminous or ex-albuminous. Nonalbuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development (e.g., pea, groundnut). Albuminous seeds retain a part of endosperm as it is not completely used up during embryo development (e.g., wheat, maize, barley, castor). Occasionally, in some seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of nucellus are also persistent.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the function of the micropyle in the seed coat?
options: To protect the seed from pests
To facilitate the entry of oxygen and water
questions.solution: Integuments of ovules harden as tough protective seed coats .The micropyle remains as a small pore in the seed coat. This facilitates entry of oxygen and water into the seed during germination. As the seed matures, its water content is reduced and seeds become relatively dry (10-15 per cent moisture by mass). The general metabolic activity of the embryo slows down. The embryo may enter a state of inactivity called dormancy, or if favourable conditions are available (adequate moisture, oxygen and suitable temperature), they germinate. As ovules mature into seeds, the ovary develops into a fruit, i.e., the transformation of ovules into seeds and ovary into fruit proceeds simultaneously. The wall of the ovary develops into the wall of fruit called pericarp. The fruits may be fleshy as in guava, orange, mango, etc., or may be dry, as in groundnut, and mustard, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What are fruits called that develop with the contribution of the thalamus in addition to the ovary?
questions.solution: In most plants, by the time the fruit develops from the ovary, other floral parts degenerate and fall off. However, in a few species such as apple, strawberry, cashew, etc., the thalamus also contributes to fruit formation. Such fruits are called false fruits (Figure 1.15b). Most fruits however develop only from the ovary and are called true fruits. Although in most of the species, fruits are the results of fertilisation, there are a few species in which fruits develop without fertilisation. Such fruits are called parthenocarpic fruits. Banana is one such example. Parthenocarpy can be induced through the application of growth hormones and such fruits are seedless. Seeds offer several advantages to angiosperms. Firstly, sincereproductive processes such as pollination and fertilisation are independent of water, seed formation is more dependable.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the term used to describe fruit production without fertilisation?
questions.solution: Although seeds, in general are the products of fertilisation, a few flowering plants such as some species of Asteraceae and grasses, have evolved a special mechanism, to produce seeds without fertilisation, called apomixis. What is fruit production without fertilisation called? Thus, apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction. There are several ways of development of apomictic seeds. In some species, the diploid egg cell is formed without reduction division and develops into the embryo without fertilisation. More often, as in many Citrus and Mango varieties some of the nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac start dividing, protrude into the embryo sac and develop into the embryos. In such species each ovule contains many embryos. Occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed is referred to as polyembryony.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is one major problem associated with hybrid seeds?
options: They need to be produced every year
questions.solution: Hybrid varieties of several of our food and vegetable crops are being extensively cultivated. Cultivation of hybrids has tremendously increased productivity. One of the problems of hybrids is that hybrid seeds have to be produced every year. If the seeds collected from hybrids are sown, the plants in the progeny will segregate and do not maintain hybrid characters. Production of hybrid seeds is costly and hence the cost of hybrid seeds become too expensive for the farmers. If these hybrids are made into apomicts, there is no segregation of characters in the hybrid progeny. Because of the importance of apomixis in hybrid seed industry, active research is going on in many laboratories around the world to understand the genetics of apomixis and to transfer apomictic genes into hybrid varieties.

options: Mature seeds may be Non-albuminous seeds that have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development (e.g., castor, groundnut).

questions.solution: Mature seeds may be non-albuminous or ex-albuminous. Non- albuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development (e.g., pea, groundnut). Albuminous seeds retain a part of the endosperm as it is not completely used up during embryo development (e.g., wheat, maize, barley, castor). As the seed matures, its water content is reduced and seeds become relatively dry (10-15 per cent moisture by mass). In most plants, by the time the fruit develops from the ovary, other floral parts degenerate and fall off. Although in most of the species, fruits are the results of fertilisation, there are a few species in which fruits develop without fertilisation. Such fruits are called parthenocarpic fruits. Bananas are one such example.

options: The inner wall of the pollen grain is called the exine.

In over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at this 2-celled stage. In the remaining species, the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to the two male gametes before pollen grains are shed (3-celled stage).

questions.solution: The inner wall of the pollen grain is called the intine. It is a thin and continuous layer made up of cellulose and pectin. The cytoplasm of pollen grain is surrounded by a plasma membrane. When the pollen grain is mature it contains two cells, the vegetative cell and generative cell (Figure 1.5b). The vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant  food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus. The generative cell is small and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell. It is spindle shaped with dense cytoplasm and a nucleus. In over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at this 2-celled stage. In the remaining species, the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to the two male gametes before pollen grains are shed (3-celled stage).

questions.solution: Autogamy in such flowers requires synchrony in pollen release and stigma receptivity and also, the anthers and the stigma should lie close to each other so that self-pollination can occur. Some plants such as Viola (common pansy), Oxalis, and Commelina produce two types of flowers –chasmogamous flowers which are similar to flowers of other species with exposed anthers and stigma, and cleistogamous flowers which do not open at all (Figure 1.9c). In such flowers, the anthers and stigma lie close to each other. When anthers dehisce in the flower buds, pollen grains come in contact with the stigma to affect pollination. Thus, cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous as there is no chance of cross-pollen landing on the stigma. Cleistogamous flowers produce assured seed-set even in the absence of pollinators.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The egg apparatus consists of one synergid and two egg cells
Reason: The synergids have special thin cellular linings which helps to guide the pollen tube into the synergid
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The egg apparatus consists of two synergids and one egg cell. The synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called filiform apparatus which helps to guide the pollen tube into the synergid

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: In embryo sac, three cells are at the chalazal end are called the antipodals
Reason: A typical angiosperm embryo sac, at maturity, though 8- nucleate is 7- celled
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In embryo sac, three cells are at the chalazal end are called the antipodals. A typical angiosperm embryo sac, at maturity, though 8- nucleate is 7- celled

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a pistil is termed pollination
Reason: Depending on the source of pollen, pollination can be divided into three types, autogamy, geitonogamy and Xenogamy
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a pistil is termed pollination. Depending on the source of pollen, pollination can be divided into three types, autogamy, geitonogamy and Xenogamy

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Autogamy in flowers requires synchrony in pollen release and stigma receptivity and also, the anthers and the stigma should lie close to each other
Reason: In autogamy, pollination is achieved within the same flower, transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In autogamy, pollination is achieved within the same flower, transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower. Autogamy in such flowers requires synchrony in pollen release and stigma receptivity and also, the anthers and the stigma should lie close to eachother so that self-pollination can occur

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Chasmogamous flowers are flowers which do not open at all
Reason: Cleistogamous flowers are flowers which are similar to flowers of other species with exposed anthers and stigma
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Cleistogamous flowers are flowers which do not open at all. Chasmogamous flowers are flowers which are similar to flowers of other species with exposed anthers and stigma

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Cleistogamous flowers produce assured seed-set even in the absence of pollinators
Reason: Some examples of plants producing Chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers are Lily, sunflower, rose, etc
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Cleistogamous flowers produce assured seed-set even in the absence of pollinators. Some examples of plants producing Chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers are Viola, Oxalis and Commelina etc

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant is geitonogamy
Reason: Although geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination involving pollinating agent, genetically it is similar to autogamy since the pollen grains come from the same plant
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant is geitonogamy. Although geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination involving pollinating agent, genetically it is similar to autogamy since the pollen grains come from the same plant

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Transfer of pollen grains from anther to the stigma of a different plant is geitonogamy
Reason: In Xenogamy, there is no genetic variation in the flowers
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Transfer of pollen grains from anther to the stigma of a different plant is Xenogamy. This is the only type of pollination which during pollination brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: There are several ways of development of apomictic seeds
Reason: In some species, the diploid egg cell is formed without reduction division and develops into the embryo without Fertilization
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: There are several ways of development of apomictic seeds. In some species, the diploid egg cell is formed without reduction division and develops into the embryo without fertilization

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Plants use two abiotic (wind and water) and one biotic agents(animals) to achieve pollination
Reason: Pollen grains coming in contact with the stigma is a chance factor in both wind and water pollination
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Plants use two abiotic (wind and water) and one biotic agents(animals) to achieve pollination. Pollen grains coming in contact with the stigma is a chance factor in both wind and water pollination

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Wind pollination requires that the pollen grains are light and non-sticky so that they can be transported in wind currents
Reason: Wind pollinated flowers often have many ovules in each ovary and very less flowers in an inflorescence
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Wind pollination requires that the pollen grains are light and non-sticky so that they can be transported in wind currents. Wind pollinated flowers often have a single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed into an inflorescence

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Wind pollinated plants often possess well-exposed stamens and large often-feathery stigma to easily trap air-borne pollen grains
Reason: Wind pollination is often common in grasses
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Wind pollinated plants often possess well-exposed stamens and large often-feathery stigma to easily trap air-borne pollen grains. Wind pollination is often common in grasses

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: In Citrus and Mango varieties each ovule contains many embryos, occurance of more than one embryo in a seed is referred to as polyembryony
Reason: In species such as Citrus and Mango varieties of the nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac start dividing, protrude into the embryo sac and develop into the embryos
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In species such as Citrus and Mango varieties of the nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac start dividing, protrude into the embryo sac and develop into the embryos. In such species each ovule contains many embryos, occurance of more than one embryo in a seed is referred to as polyembryony

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Pollination by water is quite common in dicotyledonous plants
Reason: Some examples of water pollinated plants are Zostera which grow in fresh water and several marine sea grasses such as Vallisneria and Hydrilla
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Pollination by water is quite common in monocotyledonous plants.vSome examples of water pollinated plants are Vallisneria and Hydrilla which grow in fresh water and several marine sea grasses such as Zostera

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in most of the land plants
Reason: In Vallisneria, the female flower reach the surface of water by the long stalk and the male flowers or pollen grains are released on to the surface of water
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in most of the land plants. In Vallisneria, the female flower reach the surface of water by the long stalk and the male flowers or pollen grains are released on to the surface of water

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: In another group of water pollinated plants such as sea grasses, female flowers remain submerged in water and the pollen grains are released inside the water
Reason: In most water pollinated species, pollen grains are protected from drying by a mucilaginous covering
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In another group of water pollinated plants such as sea grasses, female flowers remain submerged in water and the pollen grains are released inside the water. In most water pollinated species, pollen grains are protected from wetting by a mucilaginous covering

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Bees, butterflies, flies, beetles, wasps, ants, moths, birds and bats are the common pollinating agents
Reason: Among the animals, insects, particularly bees are the dominant biotic pollinating agents
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Bees, butterflies, flies, beetles, wasps, ants, moths, birds and bats are the common pollinating agents . Among the animals, insects, particularly bees are the dominant biotic pollinating agents

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The flowers pollinated by flies and beetles secrete fragrance to attract these animals
Reason: To prevent animal visits, the flowers have to provide rewards to the animals.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The flowers pollinated by flies and beetles secrete foul odours to attract these animals. To sustain animal visits, the flowers have to provide rewards to the animals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: In some species floral rewards are in providing safe places to lay eggs; an example is that of the tallest flower of Amorphophallus.
Reason: A similar relationship exists between a species of moth and the plant Yucca where both species-moth and the plant - cannot complete their life cycles without each other.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In some species floral rewards are in providing safe places to lay eggs; an example is that of the tallest flower of Amorphophallus. A similar relationship exists between a species of moth and the plant Yucca where both species-moth and the plant - cannot complete their life cycles without each other.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Majority of flowering plants produce hermaphrodite flowers and pollen grains are likely to come in contact with the stigma of the same flower
Reason: Continued self-pollination result in outbreeding depression
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Majority of flowering plants produce hermaphrodite flowers and pollen grains are likely to come in contact with the stigma of the same flower. Continued self-pollination result in inbreeding depression

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Self-incompatibility is the device to induce inbreeding
Reason: Self-incompatibility is a non-genetic mechanism and prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Self-incompatibility is the device to induce inbreeding. Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism and prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: A device to prevent self-pollination is the production of unisexual flowers
Reason: If both male and female flowers are present on the same plant such as rice and wheat, it prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: A device to prevent self-pollination is the production of unisexual flowers. If both male and female flowers are present on the same plant such as maize and castor, it prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: If both male and female flowers are present on the same plant such as castor and maize, it prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy
Reason: In several species such as papaya, male and female flowers are present on different plants, that is each plant is either male or female. This condition prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: If both male and female flowers are present on the same plant such as castor and maize, it prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy. In several species such as papaya, male and female flowers are present on different plants, that is each plant is either male or female. This condition prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Pollination guarantees the transfer of the right type of pollen.
Reason: The pistil does not have the ability to recognise the pollen, whether it is of the right type or of the wrong type.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Pollination does not guarantees the transfer of the right type of pollen. The pistil has the ability to recognise the pollen, whether it is of the right type or of the wrong type.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The ability of the pistil to recognise the pollen followed by its acceptance or rejection is the result of a continuous dialogue between pollen grain and the pistil
Reason: This dialogue is mediated by chemical components of the pollen interacting with those of the pistil
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The ability of the pistil to recognise the pollen followed by its acceptance or rejection is the result of a continuous dialogue between pollen grain and the pistil. This dialogue is mediated by chemical components of the pollen interacting with those of the pistil

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The pollen grain germinates on the stigma to produce a pollen tube through one of the germ pores
Reason: Pollen tube grows through the tissues of the stigma only and reaches the ovary
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The pollen grain germinates on the stigma to produce a pollen tube through one of the germ pores. Pollen tube grows through the tissues of the stigma and style and reaches the ovary

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: All the events from pollen deposition on the stigma until pollen tubes enter the ovule- are together referred to as pollen-pistil interaction
Reason: Pollen-pistil is a non dynamic process involving pollen recognition followed by promotion or inhibition of the pollen
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: All the events from pollen deposition on the stigma until pollen tubes enter the ovule- are together referred to as pollen-pistil interaction. Pollen-pistil is a dynamic process involving pollen recognition followed by promotion or inhibition of the pollen

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Artificial hybridization is one of the major approaches of crop improvement programme
Reason: In such crossing experiments it is important to make sure that only the desired pollen grains are used for pollination and the stigma is protected from contamination.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Artificial hybridization is one of the major approaches of crop improvement programme. In such crossing experiments it is important to make sure that only the desired pollen grains are used for pollination and the stigma is protected from contamination.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The female gamete moves towards the two polar nuclei located in the central cell and fuses with them to produce a triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN)
Reason: The zygote develops into an embryo while the primary endosperm cell develops into an embryo
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The male gamete moves towards the two polar nuclei located in the central cell and fuses with them to produce a triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN). The primary endosperm cell develops into the endosperm while the zygote develops into an embryo

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Following double fertilisation, events of endosperm and embryo development, maturation of ovule into seed and ovary into fruit are collectively termed post-fertilization events
Reason: The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly and forms a triploid endosperm tissue.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Following double fertilisation, events of endosperm and embryo development, maturation of ovule into seed and ovary into fruit are collectively termed post-fertilization events. The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly and forms a triploid endosperm tissue.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The cells of the endosperm tissue lacks nutrients hence cannot serve nutrition to the developing embryo
Reason: The number of free nuclei formed before cellularisation remains same
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The cells of the endosperm tissue are filled with reserve food materials and are used for nutrition of the developing embryo. The number of free nuclei formed before cellularisation varies greatly

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Endosperm may either be completely consumed by the developing embryo as in pea, groundnut, beans
Reason: The endosperm persists in the mature seed as in rice and maize and be used up during seed germination
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Endosperm may either be completely consumed by the developing embryo as in pea, groundnut, beans. The endosperm persists in the mature seed as in castor and coconut and be used up during seed germination

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: In the most common type of endosperm development, the PEN undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give rise to free nuclei
Reason: The coconut water from tender coconut is free nuclear endosperm and the surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In the most common type of endosperm development, the PEN undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give rise to free nuclei. The coconut water from tender coconut is free nuclear endosperm and the surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Zygote develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac where the embryo is situated
Reason: The early stages of embryo development are different in both monocotyledons and dicotyledons
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Embryo develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac where the zygote is situated. The early stages of embryo development are similar in both monocotyledons and dicotyledons

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The zygote gives rise to the proembryo and subsequently to the globular, heart-shaped and mature embryo
Reason: A typical dicotyledonous embryo, consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The zygote gives rise to the proembryo and subsequently to the globular, heart-shaped and mature embryo. A typical dicotyledonous embryo, consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The portion of embryonal axis above the level of cotyledons is the hypocotyl, which terminates with the radicle or root tip.
Reason: The cylindrical portion below the level of cotyledons is epicotyl that terminates at its lower end in the plumule or shoot tip
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The portion of embryonal axis above the level of cotyledons is the epicotyl, which terminates with the plumule or shoot tip. The cylindrical portion below the level of cotyledons is hypocotyl that terminates at its lower end in the radicle or root tip

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: In the grass family the cotyledon is called scutellum that is situated towards one side of the embryonal axis
Reason: At its lower end, the embryonal axis has the radicle and root cap enclosed in an undifferentiated sheath called coleorrhiza
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In the grass family the cotyledon is called scutellum that is situated towards one side of the embryonal axis. At its lower end, the embryonal axis has the radicle and root cap enclosed in an undifferentiated sheath called coleorrhiza

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Non-albuminous seeds retain a part of endosperm as it is not completely used up during embryo development as in wheat, maize, barley, castor
Reason: Albuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development as in pea and groundnut
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Albuminous seeds retain a part of endosperm as it is not completely used up during embryo development as in wheat, maize, barley, castor. Non-albuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development as in pea and groundnut

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: In some seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of nucellus are also present, known as perisperm
Reason: The micropyle remains as a small pore in the seed coat which facilitates entry of oxygen and water into the seed during germination
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In some seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of nucellus are also present, known as perisperm. The micropyle remains as a small pore in the seed coat which facilitates entry of oxygen and water into the seed during germination

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The general metabolic activity of the embryo fastens as it matures
Reason: All the seeds germinate after attaining maturity
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: As the seed matures, the general metabolic activity of the embryo slows down. The embryo may enter a state of inactivity called dormancy, or if favourable conditions are available, they germinate

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: As ovules mature into seeds, the ovary develops into a fruit
Reason: The transformation of ovules into seeds and ovary into fruit proceeds at intervals of 30 minutes
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: As ovules mature into seeds, the ovary develops into a fruit. The transformation of ovules into seeds and ovary into fruit proceeds simultaneously

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The wall of the ovary develops into the wall of fruit called pericarp

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological sequence regarding the development of a mature male gametophyte from a microspore mother cell (MMC) in a typical angiosperm:

I. Asymmetric mitotic division of the microspore nucleus.
II. Meiotic division of the microspore mother cell.
III. Dissociation of the microspore tetrad.
IV. Mitotic division of the generative cell to form two male gametes.
V. Formation of a large vegetative cell and a small generative cell.
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 6 - 7 | Paragraph: 1 - 2

The development of a mature male gametophyte from a microspore mother cell (MMC) in a typical angiosperm follows a specific sequence of events:

The microspore mother cell (MMC) first undergoes meiotic division to form a cluster of four cells called a microspore tetrad (Event II).

As the anther matures and dehydrates, the microspores dissociate from the tetrad and develop into individual pollen grains (Event III).

Inside the pollen grain, the microspore nucleus undergoes an asymmetric mitotic division (Event I).

This asymmetric division results in the formation of two unequal cells: a large vegetative cell and a small spindle-shaped generative cell (Event V).

Finally, the generative cell undergoes a second mitotic division to produce two non-motile male gametes, completing the formation of a mature three-celled male gametophyte (Event IV).

The correct chronological sequence is II → III → I → V → IV.

Answer: II → III → I → V → IV

questions.solution: Typical dicotyledonous embryo (Figure 1.14a), consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons. The portion of embryonal axis above the level of cotyledons is the epicotyl, which terminates with the plumule or stem tip. questions.solution: Embryos of monocotyledons (Figure 1.14 b) possess only one cotyledon. In the grass family the cotyledon is called scutellum that is situated towards one side (lateral) of the embryonal axis. At its lower end, the embryonal axis has the radical and root cap enclosed in an undifferentiated sheath called coleorrhiza. The portion of the embryonal axis above the level of attachment of scutellum is the epicotyl. Epicotyl has a shoot apex and a few leaf primordia enclosed in a hollow foliar structure, the coleoptile.

questions.solution: Artificial hybridisation is one of the major approaches of crop improvement programme. In such crossing experiments it is important to make sure that only the desired pollen grains are used for pollination and the stigma is protected from contamination (from unwanted pollen). Emasculated flowers have to be covered with a bag of suitable size, generally made up of butter paper, to prevent contamination of its stigma with unwanted pollen. This process is called bagging. When the stigma of bagged flower attains receptivity, mature pollen grains collected from anthers of the male parent are dusted on the stigma, and the flowers are rebagged, and the fruits allowed to develop.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the correct developmental sequence related to megasporogenesis and female gametophyte formation in angiosperms :
A. Megaspore tetrad
B. Megaspore mother cell
C. Embryo sac
D. Functional megaspore
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
During megasporogenesis, a single cell in the nucellus differentiates into a diploid Megaspore Mother Cell (MMC). The MMC undergoes meiotic division to form a linear Megaspore tetrad (four haploid megaspores). In a majority of angiosperms, three megaspores degenerate and one remains as the Functional megaspore. This functional megaspore then undergoes mitotic divisions to develop into the female gametophyte, which is the Embryo sac.

The correct developmental sequence is:
Megaspore mother cell → Megaspore tetrad → Functional megaspore → Embryo sac.

This corresponds to the sequence B, A, D, C.

Answer: B, A, D, C

(D) All seedless fruits develop from the thalamus.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct because in false fruits like apple, strawberry, and cashew, the thalamus contributes to fruit formation.

Statement (B) is correct because parthenocarpy can be induced artificially by the application of growth hormones, resulting in seedless fruits.

Statement (C) is incorrect because mango is a true fruit that develops only from the ovary.

Statement (D) is incorrect because seedless fruits are parthenocarpic fruits which develop from the ovary without fertilization, whereas the involvement of the thalamus is a characteristic of false fruits.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
A. The hard outer layer of the pollen grain called exine is made up of sporopollenin which can withstand high temperatures.
B. The inner wall of the pollen grain, intine, is a continuous layer made up of cellulose and pectin.
C. The innermost wall layer of the microsporangium, tapetum, helps in the dehiscence of anther to release the pollen.
D. Sporopollenin can be degraded by specific enzymes at high temperatures.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct: The exine is the hard outer layer of the pollen grain, composed of sporopollenin, which is highly resistant to high temperatures, strong acids, and alkalis.

Statement B is correct: The intine is the inner wall of the pollen grain. It is a thin, continuous layer made up of cellulose and pectin.

Statement C is incorrect: The tapetum is the innermost wall layer of the microsporangium, but its primary function is to nourish the developing pollen grains. The outer three layers (epidermis, endothecium, and middle layers) perform the function of protection and help in the dehiscence of the anther.

Statement D is incorrect: Sporopollenin is one of the most resistant organic materials known. No enzyme that degrades sporopollenin is so far known.

Therefore, exactly two statements (A and B) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the development of a typical female gametophyte in angiosperms:
(A) The method of embryo sac formation from a single megaspore is termed monosporic development.
(B) The mitotic divisions of the functional megaspore are strictly free-nuclear.
(C) Cell wall formation occurs immediately after every mitotic division.
(D) Six of the eight nuclei are surrounded by cell walls and organized into cells.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as the development of an embryo sac from a single functional megaspore is called monosporic development.

Statement (B) is correct because the mitotic divisions during megagametogenesis are strictly free-nuclear, meaning nuclear divisions are not immediately followed by cell wall formation.

Statement (C) is incorrect because cell walls are not laid down immediately after every division; they are formed only after the 8-nucleate stage is reached, leading to the organization of the typical female gametophyte.

Statement (D) is correct as six of the eight nuclei are surrounded by cell walls to form the egg apparatus (3 cells) and antipodals (3 cells), while the remaining two polar nuclei share the large central cell.

Thus, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Only three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

List IList II
A. PerispermI. Wall of the fruit
B. PericarpII. Encloses the shoot apex
C. TestaIII. Remnant of nucellus
D. ColeoptileIV. Outer seed coat


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Perisperm (A) is the residual, persistent nucellus found in certain seeds like black pepper and beet (Matches with III).

Pericarp (B) is the wall of the fruit that develops from the wall of the ovary after fertilization (Matches with I).

Testa (C) is the outer layer of the seed coat, which develops from the outer integument of the ovule (Matches with IV).

Coleoptile (D) is a hollow foliar structure in monocot embryos that encloses the shoot apex and leaf primordia (Matches with II).

Option 1 is incorrect because it swaps the definitions of perisperm and pericarp. Option 3 incorrectly matches testa with the shoot apex enclosure. Option 4 incorrectly identifies perisperm as the outer seed coat.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Pollen grains of cereals like wheat and rice lose viability within 30 minutes of their release.
Reason (R): In some members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae and Solanaceae, pollen grains lose viability within a few hours.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because in cereals such as rice and wheat, pollen grains lose viability within 30 minutes of their release.

Reason (R) is false because in some members of families like Rosaceae, Leguminosae and Solanaceae, pollen grains maintain viability for months, rather than losing it within a few hours.

Therefore, Assertion is true but Reason is false.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Microspore tetrads formed inside the microsporangium are haploid in nature.
Reason (R): They are formed by the mitotic division of diploid pollen mother cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because microspore tetrads consist of four microspores, which are haploid (n) cells.

Reason (R) is false because microspore tetrads are formed by the meiotic (reductional) division of diploid pollen mother cells (PMCs), not by mitotic division. Meiosis ensures that the resulting microspores are haploid.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Apple and strawberry are classified as false fruits.
Reason (R): They develop without the process of fertilization and are naturally seedless.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because in apple and strawberry, the thalamus contributes to fruit formation, which is the defining characteristic of false fruits.

Reason (R) is incorrect because false fruits still develop after fertilization and contain seeds. Fruits that develop without fertilization and are naturally seedless are called parthenocarpic fruits (e.g., banana). A common misconception is conflating false fruits with parthenocarpic fruits.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Read the following statements regarding double fertilization in angiosperms and choose the incorrect statement.
options: The central cell after triple fusion becomes the primary endosperm cell and develops into the endosperm.
The synergids and antipodals degenerate after fertilization.
The primary endosperm nucleus is formed by syngamy and develops into the embryo.
Prior to fertilization, the large central cell of the embryo sac contains two polar nuclei.
questions.solution:
In angiosperms, double fertilization involves two distinct fusion events: syngamy and triple fusion.

Syngamy is the fusion of one male gamete with the egg cell to form a diploid zygote, which subsequently develops into the embryo.

Triple fusion is the fusion of the second male gamete with the two polar nuclei in the central cell to form a triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN). Following this, the central cell becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into the endosperm.

Therefore, the statement claiming that the primary endosperm nucleus is formed by syngamy and develops into the embryo is incorrect. The other statements accurately describe the post-fertilization fate of the central cell, the degeneration of synergids and antipodals, and the pre-fertilization state of the central cell.

Answer: The primary endosperm nucleus is formed by syngamy and develops into the embryo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding pollination and outbreeding devices:
(I) In some species, pollen release and stigma receptivity are not synchronised to prevent autogamy.
(II) Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules.
(III) In papaya, male and female flowers are present on the same plant, preventing geitonogamy.
(IV) Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination but genetically similar to autogamy.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct: Lack of synchronisation between pollen release and stigma receptivity is an outbreeding device that prevents autogamy.

Statement (II) is correct: Self-incompatibility is a genetically mediated mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.

Statement (III) is incorrect: Papaya is a dioecious plant, meaning male and female flowers are present on different plants. This condition prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy. Plants with male and female flowers on the same plant are monoecious (e.g., castor and maize).

Statement (IV) is correct: Geitonogamy involves the transfer of pollen to the stigma of another flower of the same plant. It requires a pollinating agent (making it functionally cross-pollination) but the pollen grains come from the same plant (making it genetically similar to autogamy).

Therefore, three statements (I, II, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding pollination adaptations:

List-IList-II
A. Light and non-sticky pollen grainsI. Seagrasses (e.g., Zostera)
B. Long, ribbon-like pollen grainsII. Most water-pollinated species
C. Pollen grains protected by mucilaginous coveringIII. Insect-pollinated plants
D. Flowers produce nectar and are fragrantIV. Wind-pollinated plants


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, wind-pollinated plants produce light and non-sticky pollen grains so they can be easily transported by wind currents.

In seagrasses such as Zostera, female flowers remain submerged in water, and the pollen grains are long and ribbon-like, carried passively inside the water.

In most water-pollinated species, pollen grains are protected from wetting by a mucilaginous covering.

Insect-pollinated flowers are typically large, colourful, fragrant, and rich in nectar to attract animal pollinators.

Thus, the correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the components of a typical angiosperm embryo sac.

List-IList-II
A. SynergidsI. Contains polar nuclei
B. Egg cellII. Located at chalazal end
C. Central cellIII. Possess filiform apparatus
D. AntipodalsIV. Female gamete

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
A typical angiosperm embryo sac consists of an egg apparatus at the micropylar end, three antipodal cells at the chalazal end, and a large central cell.

The egg apparatus comprises two synergids and one egg cell (the female gamete). The synergids possess special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus.

The central cell is the largest cell of the embryo sac and contains two polar nuclei.

The antipodals are three cells located at the chalazal end.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the chalaza in a typical angiosperm ovule?
options: It represents the junction between the ovule body and the funicle.
It represents the basal part of the ovule opposite to the micropylar end.
It is the narrow pore or passage at the tip where the integuments are absent.
It is the central parenchymatous mass of tissue containing abundant food reserve.
questions.solution:
The chalaza represents the basal part of the ovule and is located opposite to the micropylar end.

The other options describe different structures of the ovule:
The junction between the ovule body and the funicle is the hilum.
The narrow pore where the integuments are absent is the micropyle.
The central parenchymatous mass of tissue enclosed within the integuments is the nucellus.

Answer: It represents the basal part of the ovule opposite to the micropylar end.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the reproductive features of plants.

List-IList-II
(A) Papaya(1) Prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy
(B) Castor(2) Prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy
(C) Commelina(3) Produces both chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Papaya is a dioecious plant, meaning male and female flowers are present on different plants. This condition prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy. Thus, (A) matches with (2).

Castor is a monoecious plant, where male and female flowers are borne on the same plant. This prevents autogamy (pollination within the same flower) but not geitonogamy (pollination between different flowers of the same plant). Thus, (B) matches with (1).

Commelina produces two types of flowers: chasmogamous flowers (similar to flowers of other species with exposed anthers and stigma) and cleistogamous flowers (which do not open at all). Thus, (C) matches with (3).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(2), (B)-(1), (C)-(3).

Answer: (A)-(2), (B)-(1), (C)-(3)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A cross is made between a male angiospermic plant with a diploid chromosome number of $16$ and a female plant with a diploid chromosome number of $24$. What will be the chromosome number in the endosperm and the embryo, respectively, of the resulting seeds?
questions.solution:
The diploid chromosome number of the male parent is $2n = 16$. Therefore, the haploid male gamete will have $n = 8$ chromosomes.

The diploid chromosome number of the female parent is $2n = 24$. Therefore, the haploid egg cell will have $n = 12$ chromosomes, and the diploid secondary nucleus (formed by the fusion of two haploid polar nuclei) will have $2n = 24$ chromosomes.

The embryo is formed by syngamy, which is the fusion of one male gamete and the egg cell. The chromosome number in the embryo will be $8 + 12 = 20$.

The endosperm is formed by triple fusion, where the second male gamete fuses with the secondary nucleus. The chromosome number in the endosperm will be $8 + 24 = 32$.

Thus, the chromosome numbers in the endosperm and the embryo are $32$ and $20$, respectively.

Answer: $32$ and $20$

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The perisperm observed in the mature seeds of black pepper and beet is anatomically distinct from the endosperm.
Reason (R): Perisperm is the persistent remnant of nucellus, whereas endosperm develops from the primary endosperm nucleus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect.
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because perisperm and endosperm are two different nutritive tissues found in seeds. Black pepper and beet are classic examples of seeds possessing perisperm.

Reason (R) is also correct and correctly explains the Assertion. Perisperm represents the residual, persistent nucellus (diploid maternal tissue) in the seed. In contrast, endosperm is a newly formed tissue that develops from the triploid primary endosperm nucleus after double fertilization. Because they have entirely different developmental origins, they are anatomically distinct.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
